null-vs-empty.notApplicableReason: Every text column this procedure reads (Sales.OrderLines.Description, Warehouse.PackageTypes.PackageTypeName) is NOT NULL, so no NULL text value can be sent. '' is sent as a Description in the text case.

cases.label: the later of order and line time decides: order inside with line after @NewCutoff (excluded); order after @NewCutoff with line inside (excluded); both at @NewCutoff (included); later time exactly @LastCutoff (excluded)
cases.reasoning: Last Modified When is the later of the two LastEditedWhen values and both bounds apply to it. Order 1 is in the window but its line is 1 µs after @NewCutoff; order 2 is 1 µs after @NewCutoff with its line inside; order 3 and its line are both exactly @NewCutoff; order 4's later time is exactly @LastCutoff. A conversion that filtered the order and the line separately, or used the earlier time, would differ.

cases.label: one order, lines edited at different times: only the lines whose later time is inside the window are listed
cases.reasoning: Order 1 was edited before the window. Line 1 is 1 µs after @LastCutoff (in), line 2 1 µs after @NewCutoff (out), line 3 exactly @NewCutoff (in), line 4 exactly @LastCutoff (out). The listed rows share WWI Order ID and every order column; ORDER BY o.OrderID does not order them further.

cases.label: tax rounds half away from zero at 2 places, also for negative quantities: 0.005 -> 0.01, -0.105 -> -0.11, 1.2075 -> 1.21, 0.087535 -> 0.09, 14994998.5005 -> 14994998.50
cases.reasoning: ROUND(Quantity * UnitPrice * TaxRate / 100.0, 2) on decimal rounds half away from zero; PostgreSQL round(numeric) does too, but trunc() or a float round-half-even would not. Quantity -3 makes the tax and both totals negative; 1000 x 99999.99 x 14.995 checks a large product.

cases.label: SQL Server's decimal scale: Quantity x UnitPrice x TaxRate / 100.0 is decimal(38,6), so 0.0049999 becomes 0.004999 before ROUND; NULL UnitPrice and a zero rate
cases.reasoning: The product int x decimal(18,2) x decimal(18,3) exceeds precision 38, and the division by 100.0 is cut to scale 6 on SQL Server; PostgreSQL keeps all digits. 0.0049999 and 0.0050001 sit on either side of the 2-place midpoint. UnitPrice NULL gives NULL for every total; TaxRate 0.000 gives a tax of 0.00.

cases.label: text as stored: descriptions differing only in case or by a trailing space, an empty description, an emoji; a package name with a trailing space
cases.reasoning: Nothing is compared on text; Description and Package must keep their spelling. 'Widget', 'WIDGET' and 'widget ' are three lines; '' is not NULL; the emoji is a surrogate pair in nvarchar(100). Package 'Bag ' keeps its space (package names stay distinct under the unique name).

cases.label: dates at the limits: OrderDate 1753-01-01 and 9999-12-31; PickingCompletedWhen 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999, 1753-01-01 00:00:00 and NULL
cases.reasoning: CAST(... AS date) of 9999-12-31 23:59:59.999999 must keep 9999-12-31 (a rounding conversion would overflow); 1753-01-01 is the datetime minimum many converters assume; NULL picking time gives a NULL Picked Date Key.

cases.label: inner joins and keys: an unknown package type and an unknown customer drop their rows; an order without lines; ids with gaps and at the int limits
cases.reasoning: Order 2147483647's line uses package type 9 (missing): dropped. Order 1000's customer 77 is missing: dropped. Order 5 has no lines. Order -2147483648 has a backorder id and a picker. WWI City ID comes from the customer row (city 2147483647).
